Four passes asked for this and *"no action among the eighteen names it."* - ⚠ **RESTATED 2026-08-29 — this is a breadth task, not a sensitivity task. See F76.** The premise that the one-file corpus means *"the instrument has not been shown able to fail"* is **false** and was inherited by this very file when it was written. The contract is calibrated: all twelve assertions have a known-bad, enforced by `tests/test_connector_contract.py::test_every_assertion_has_been_proved_able_to_fail`, and `certify --calibrate` now returns `PASS (PASS=12)` — not the `UNMEASURABLE (PASS=11)` the README claimed until today. What one fixture cannot show is that the contract **generalises**: it has been replayed against one connector, and 48 have never been scored.

AB-19.acc: re-decide with all five positions on the table, and record the decision with its dissent. --- ## Closing rule A row closes when its **ACTION** is done *or* when a written rejection exists naming the row. Both outcomes are progress. What is not progress — and what produced this file — is a row that is mentioned in a synthesis and mistaken for one that was handled.

CIP-01.why: Nineteen conclusions that named a mechanism and never reached the decision record. A written reject closes one as legitimately as a build does.
CIP-01.acc: Every AB row carries DO / REJECT / MERGE and a one-line reason. Zero rows left unjudged.

CIP-02.why: A gap register judged against a stated objective, so “missing” means missing relative to something.
CIP-02.acc: Every gap names the answer that should have covered it, by file and section.

CIP-03.why: A pilot chosen for convenience proves nothing transferable. State the selection reason so a failure is interpretable.
CIP-03.acc: One connector named, with the reason it is representative and what it will not prove.

CIP-04.why: The record is the artefact everything else checks. One real one beats a template nobody filled.
CIP-04.acc: Passes check_intake.py --stage commit, then --stage deploy. Consumer route walked, not assumed.

CIP-05.why: Closes the loop from what the client declared to what actually landed.
CIP-05.acc: certify returns PASS on all twelve, and labels its own basis REPLAYED or LIVE.

CIP-06.why: The corpus holds one file. A frozen evaluator scoring n=1 cannot tell a good version from a lucky replay.
CIP-06.acc: Corpus count rises; MANIFEST.sha256 verifies; test_corpus.py green.

CIP-07.why: Entity types, relationships, roles, decision gates. The dimensions are the schema, not a style choice.
CIP-07.acc: Every question maps to one of the four; count is 20–30; none is free text without a target field.

CIP-08.why: A question whose answer nothing checks is a question that produces a hope.
CIP-08.acc: A table with three columns and no empty third cell.
CIP-08.ev: the mapping table, in the spec

CIP-09.why: 20–30 questions is at the edge of what a client will finish. Every field we can read is a field we must not ask.
CIP-09.acc: Fields derivable from the source are pre-filled and marked as probed, not asserted.
CIP-09.ev: a probe run against the pilot source

CIP-10.why: Any hand-editing step between the client's answer and the contract is where drift enters.
CIP-10.acc: A filled form produces frontmatter that passes check_intake.py with zero edits.

CIP-11.why: The client sees their own declaration reflected back as Live / Partial / Awaiting / Pending / Not-in-scope.
CIP-11.acc: Uses the existing five-term vocabulary. No sixth term invented.

CIP-12.why: Three ticket-record systems already disagree. A fourth that owns state is the failure, not the fix.
CIP-12.acc: Portal has no write path to anything but a PR. Killing the portal loses no record.

CIP-13.why: Per-client auth and row-level security are already provisioned in code. Inventing a second model is how isolation breaks.
CIP-13.acc: No new auth code. Access provisioned by the existing CLI.

CIP-14.why: Named as missing in the compounding research — the store currently accepts ~100% of writes.
CIP-14.acc: A deliberately ungrounded write is refused in a test. Rejection rate is reported, not assumed.

CIP-15.why: Retooled AOR. Compare the corpus to real demand, not to itself — comparing it to itself measures repetition.
CIP-15.acc: Judged by relevance, not cosine similarity and not outcome. Output is a ranked gap list.

CIP-16.why: Rank currently scales with retrieval_count alone, so a wrong-but-popular memory climbs and spreads its mistake.
CIP-16.acc: max(0,(uses−corrections+k)/(uses+2k)) with k≈2. The naive ratio is not shipped.
CIP-16.ev: the three worked cases from the research note

CIP-17.why: A guard blocked nothing for months because it depended on a binary that was not installed and exited the wrong code.
CIP-17.acc: Each gate proves it blocks AND proves it lets legitimate work through.

CIP-18.why: The decisive test that collapsed an 18-point signal to ~0. Without it, any improvement claim measures repetition.
CIP-18.acc: Compares like with like inside one topic cluster. Reports the control alongside the result.
CIP-18.ev: the harness, and its output on real data

CIP-19.why: A falling correction rate proves improvement only if the questions did not simply get easier.
CIP-19.acc: A controlled comparison, pre-registered before the data is seen.

CIP-20.why: The agreeing cases are the control; the divergent ones are the finding. Publishing only the wins is how a confound survives.
CIP-20.acc: Every divergence investigated and reported, including the ones that weaken the claim.

CIP-24.why: Lane naming is derived from the boot prompt rather than the work, and nothing proves the name survives the spawn. control-room.md §5 Slice 0; also raised independently as deepseek D5.
CIP-24.acc: A test spawns through the REAL launcher and reads the name back out of the registry. Until it passes, naming stays INFERRED.
CIP-24.ev: docs/specs/control-room.md §5 Slice 0; sessions.py:99; local_tracker.py:345 (sets it, nothing asserts it)

CIP-25.why: finish.checks() pairs a PER-LANE findings query with a GLOBAL nothing_to_report() count, so one NOTHING TO REPORT written by any lane permanently satisfies the check for every lane. Silence stops meaning 'checked'.
CIP-25.acc: nothing_to_report() is scoped per lane; a test proves lane B still fails the check after lane A has written one.

CIP-27.why: F72: the board's number depends on the directory it is run from (9 of 30 from the checkout, 10 of 30 from a worktree, same commit). The $PREFECT_CONNECTORS override has since landed; the cwd-relative default has not, so F72 still reproduces whenever the var is unset.
CIP-27.acc: Two halves, both required: (a) resolution no longer varies with cwd when the var is unset; (b) the HEADLINE carries its basis, so a number quoted out of context cannot read as global. Proof: same commit measured from checkout and from a worktree gives the same headline.

CIP-29.why: A measurement-scope object so a figure carries what it was measured over. ⚠ NAME COLLISION: factory/schedule.py:59 already defines `class Snapshot` — a frozen when/passed/total/sha record parsed from the artifact's git history, used only inside schedule.py.
CIP-29.acc: The new object ships under a name that does not collide, OR the two are deliberately reconciled in writing. A second `Snapshot` in the codebase is not an acceptable outcome.

CIP-36.why: The blocked-question inbox is BUILT — sessions.py:257/265/286 plus hooks/lane-attention.py for the intrusive half — but its gate has never been run. Replaces CIP-23, which asked to build what already existed. By §5's rule 'a slice with no gate is not a slice', it is not done.
CIP-36.acc: A fire drill: block a real agent on a real question and time how long until a human sees it. Before: unbounded (4 sat all day). Target: under a minute. Record the drill as evidence.
